about.title: Personal Injury Help in Commerce, California
about.longDescription: Commerce is a small but heavily traveled city, with the I-5 (Santa Ana Freeway) and Telegraph Road carrying much of the daily traffic through town. In the most recent final reporting year, Commerce recorded 254 injury collisions, 333 injured people, and 2 traffic deaths — numbers that reflect how much movement passes through a city of just over 13,000 residents. Many of these crashes cluster on Fridays between 4 and 6 p.m., when commuter and weekend traffic overlap near the freeway corridor. If you were hurt in a collision, fall, or other accident in Commerce, it helps to understand your options quickly, since California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim — and often only six months if a government entity is involved. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect injured people in Commerce with independent personal injury attorneys who can review the details of a case at no upfront cost. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover compensation on your behalf. Reaching out costs nothing and creates no obligation.

whyChoose.title: Why It Helps to Act Quickly

items.title: California's Two-Year Filing Window
items.desc: Most personal injury claims in California must be filed within two years of the incident. Claims against a government agency can require notice within six months, so timing matters.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Automatically Bar You
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible — your share of fault simply reduces the award rather than eliminating it.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California does not limit compensation for pain, suffering, and other non-economic losses, unlike some other states.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost and no fee unless they win compensation for you.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Commerce?
items.answer: California law generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file most personal injury claims. If your claim involves a government entity, such as a city vehicle, the window can be as short as six months. Because these deadlines are strict, it helps to act sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault system, so being partially responsible doesn't prevent you from recovering compensation. Your total award would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault. An independent attorney can help evaluate how fault might apply to your specific situation.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Commerce?
items.answer: Based on public-record collision counts, reported crashes in Commerce tend to cluster along the I-5 (Santa Ana Freeway) and Telegraph Road corridors, and often peak on Fridays between 4 and 6 p.m. These are simply reported patterns from crash data, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much compensation I can recover?
items.answer: In ordinary personal injury cases, California does not cap non-economic damages, such as pain and suffering. Economic damages like medical costs and lost wages are also generally recoverable without a statutory cap in standard injury claims.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with independent attorneys, and we are not a law firm ourselves. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if they recover compensation for you.
